mainTopic: לחי העומד מאליו: the dispute of אביי and רבא, whether it extends to a מחיצה, and whether a לחי is a מחיצה or a היכר
overview: The גמרא brings a dispute between אביי and רבא about a לחי העומד מאליו, a post at the entrance of a מבוי that was not put there to be a לחי. At first it says they argue only when people relied on the post from before שבת. אביי accepts it, and רבא rejects it because it was not made for this purpose. The גמרא then assumes they also argue about a מחיצה that was not made to be a wall. It tests this against a סוכה among trees, trees and reed hedges serving as a דיומד, and a low-hanging tree, and it deflects each proof by saying the items were made on purpose. A ברייתא about a natural mound and cavity cannot be deflected this way. So the גמרא reframes the dispute: everyone agrees natural walls count. אביי holds that a לחי works as a מחיצה, while רבא holds that it is a היכר, which must be made by hand. Two ברייתות about wall stones and a recessed wall are deflected, but a story about רב and a palm tree seems to support אביי. The balcony of בר חבו shows they argue even when people relied on the item. A new משנה then begins: a לחי may be made from anything, even a living creature, though רבי מאיר forbids it.

steps.title: Dispute over a side post that stands by itself
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a לחי העומד מאליו is a valid לחי. רבא says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: about a side post that stands by itself, אביי said it is a valid side post, and רבא said it is not a valid side post.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a new dispute between אביי and רבא. The question is whether a post that was already standing at the entrance of a מבוי can work as a לחי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לחי is normally put up on purpose so that people may carry in the מבוי on שבת. Here the post was simply there already. אביי accepts it as a לחי and רבא rejects it.

keyTerms.meaning: A side post at the entrance of an alleyway (מבוי) that permits carrying there
That stands by itself, meaning it was not put up for this purpose

phrases.english: It was stated:
A side post that stands by itself,
Abaye said: it is a valid side post,
Rava said: it is not a valid side post.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: לֶחִי הָעוֹמֵד מֵאֵלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in the sugya
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: a לחי העומד מאליו is valid. רבא: it is not valid.

steps.title: Narrowing where the dispute applies
steps.stepSummary: If the people did not rely on the post from before שבת, everyone agrees it is not a לחי. They argue only where they did rely on it from before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where we did not rely on it from yesterday, everyone agrees it is not a side post. Where they argue is where we did rely on it from yesterday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the dispute to one situation. Here everyone agrees; the argument applies only in the other case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take a case where the מבוי had another לחי that fell on שבת, so nobody had been relying on this post. In that case everyone agrees the post does not count. The argument applies only when the residents had been relying on this post from before שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: From yesterday, meaning from before שבת began

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי accepts every post that happens to be standing there. Even אביי agrees a post nobody relied on before שבת does not count.

phrases.english: Where we did not rely on it from yesterday,
everyone does not argue
that it is not a valid side post.
Where they do argue
is where we relied on it from yesterday.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּלָא סָמְכִינַן עֲלֵיהּ מֵאֶתְמוֹל, כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case in which the dispute of step 1 applies
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no dispute where nobody relied on the post before שבת. The dispute applies only where they did rely on it.

steps.title: The reasons of אביי and רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי: it counts because people relied on it from before שבת. רבא: it does not count because it was not originally made for this purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said it is a side post, since we relied on it from yesterday. רבא said it is not a side post, since from the start it was not made with this intention, so it is not a side post.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives each אמורא's reason for his position in the disputed case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, what matters is that people actually relied on the post as a לחי. For רבא, what matters is why the post was made in the first place. If it was not made to be a לחי, later reliance does not help.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי asks: did people rely on it? רבא asks: was it made for this purpose from the start?

phrases.english: Abaye said: it is a valid side post,
since we relied on it from yesterday.
Rava said: it is not a valid side post,
since originally
it was not made with this intention,
it is not a valid side post.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: הָוֵי לֶחִי, דְּהָא סָמְכִינַן עֲלֵיהּ מֵאֶתְמוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for each side in the case defined in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: reliance from before שבת makes it a לחי. רבא: lack of original intent means it is not a לחי.

steps.title: Assuming the dispute also applies to a partition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes that אביי and רבא would argue the same way about a מחיצה that was not made to be a wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that just as they argue about a side post, they also argue about a partition.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא states an assumption and is about to test it with a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that רבא's reasoning applies to a מחיצה too. Under that reading, a wall not made for this purpose would not count as a מחיצה according to רבא. The next step will check this.

keyTerms.meaning: It might enter your mind (a starting assumption)

phrases.english: It enters your mind
that just as they argue about a side post,
they also argue about a partition.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ כִּי הֵיכִי דִּפְלִיגִי בְּלֶחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the dispute from a לחי to a מחיצה as a working assumption
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Working assumption: the dispute about a לחי extends to a מחיצה.

steps.title: Proof from a סוכה built among trees
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a סוכה whose walls are trees is כשרה. This suggests that walls not made for the purpose still count, which seems to go against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one who makes his סוכה among the trees, and the trees are its walls, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to test the assumption of step 4. Trees serve as walls of a סוכה even though nobody made them to be walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trees are a clear case of a wall not made for this purpose. If רבא also argues about a מחיצה, he would have to say such a סוכה is invalid. The משנה says it is כשרה, so either the assumption or רבא's view seems wrong.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who makes his sukka among the trees
and the trees are its walls —
it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָעוֹשֶׂה סוּכָּתוֹ בֵּין הָאִילָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the assumption of step 4 against a משנה
steps.raayaObject: That a מחיצה not made for its purpose is valid, which challenges רבא if he also argues about a מחיצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוכה: a סוכה whose walls are trees is כשרה

steps.title: The trees were planted for this purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא deflects the proof. The משנה is speaking of trees that were planted from the start to serve as the סוכה's walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? Where he planted them from the start for this purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by narrowing the case in the משנה. This way the משנה fits רבא too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the trees were planted to be walls, they were made with the right intention from the start. Even רבא agrees they count. So the משנה proves nothing about a wall that was not made for this purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here (introduces a narrowing of the case)
From the start for this purpose

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where he planted them from the start for this purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 5 by narrowing the case
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה of the סוכה among trees
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the trees were not made to be walls. The משנה can be read as trees planted for that purpose.

steps.title: Then the משנה is obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the trees were planted to be walls, why did the משנה need to tell us the סוכה is כשרה? That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the narrowed reading of step 6. If the trees were planted for this purpose, the ruling seems too obvious to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to state something obvious. Walls deliberately made to be walls are plainly valid. So the reading of step 6 seems to leave the משנה with nothing new to teach.

phrases.english: If so, it is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the narrowed reading given in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the trees were planted for this purpose
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading the משנה's ruling is obvious, and a משנה should not teach something obvious.

steps.title: The משנה teaches there is no גזירה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed to teach that חכמים did not forbid such a סוכה out of fear that a person would use the tree on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let us make a decree, lest he come to use the tree. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 7. It explains what new information the משנה teaches even if the trees were planted for this purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a tree on יום טוב, for example climbing it or pulling off a branch or leaf, is forbidden. One might think חכמים made a גזירה against a סוכה with tree walls, since a person sitting in it might come to use the tree. The משנה teaches that no such גזירה was made, so the ruling is not obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Let us make a rabbinic decree (גזירה)
To make use of a tree (forbidden on שבת and יום טוב)

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the סוכה among trees is deflected: the trees were planted to be walls. The משנה's new point is that there is no גזירה about using the tree.

phrases.english: You might have said:
let us make a decree, lest
he come to make use of the tree,
so it teaches us that there is no such decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: לִיגְזוֹר דִּילְמָא אָתֵי לְאִישְׁתַּמּוֹשֵׁי בְּאִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a non-obvious חידוש: rejecting a possible גזירה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think חכמים forbade a סוכה with tree walls in case the person comes to use the tree on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such גזירה was made. The סוכה is כשרה, so the משנה is not obvious, and the reading of trees planted for this purpose stands.

steps.title: Proof from a tree, fence, or reeds serving as a double post
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a tree, fence, or reed hedge counts as a דיומד. These were not made to be walls, so this seems to go against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If there was a tree there, or a fence, or a hedge of reeds, it counts as a double post!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that seems to prove that a wall not made to be a wall still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Around a public well, a corner piece called a דיומד helps form the enclosure. The ברייתא says a natural tree or an existing fence or reed hedge can do that job. These things were usually not put there as walls, so this seems to support אביי and go against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A double post. It is an L-shaped corner piece used to enclose a public well.
A hedge or barrier made of reeds.
It is judged as, or counts as.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If there was a tree there
or a fence, or a barrier of reeds
it is judged as a double post!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיָה שָׁם אִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof from the סוכה was answered, the גמרא brings a new proof on the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That a wall not made to be a wall is still valid, which goes against רבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about wells, which says a tree, fence, or reed hedge counts as a דיומד.

steps.title: The items were made for this purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא deflects the proof. The ברייתא is speaking of a case where these things were set up from the start to be the double post.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, what case are we dealing with? Where he made them from the start for this purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof, the same way it did with the סוכה made of trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tree, fence, or reeds were put there in order to act as walls, then they are walls made for the purpose. Even רבא agrees that such walls count. So the proof against רבא falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too. This points back to the same answer used before.
What case are we dealing with?
From the start, for this purpose.

phrases.english: Here too, with what are we dealing?
where he made them from the start for this purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the proof of step 9, using the same move as step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It narrows the ברייתא to a specific case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the items were not made as walls. They may have been made as walls on purpose.

steps.title: Then why state the obvious?
steps.stepSummary: If they were made to be walls, it is obvious they count. So what is the ברייתא teaching?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. If the items were made as walls, the ברייתא seems to tell us nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is not supposed to state something obvious. Once we say the items were made for this purpose, the ruling seems pointless. So the deflection needs support.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? This asks what is new in the source.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן?
phrases.english: If so, what does it teach us?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It attacks the answer given in step 10, like step 7 did earlier.
steps.kashyaTarget: The deflection that the items were made for this purpose.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that is the case, the ruling is obvious. A ברייתא should teach something new.

steps.title: It teaches the rule about gaps between reeds
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that a reed hedge counts as a wall when each reed is less than three טפחים from the next. This answers a question אביי asked רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us that a reed hedge counts when the gap between one reed and the next is less than three handbreadths. This is like the question אביי asked רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא does have a new lesson, even if the items were made as walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new lesson is not about why the wall was made. It is about a hedge with gaps. If the gaps are under three טפחים, the reeds join together into one wall through לבוד. This settles a question אביי asked רבה, so the ברייתא is not stating the obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: Reed by reed. It means the gap between one reed and the next.
Less than three handbreadths. This is the size of gap that counts as closed.
As he asked of him. This points to a question asked earlier.

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's new lesson is not that the reeds were made as walls. It is about how far apart the reeds may be and still count as one wall.

phrases.english: It teaches us
that a barrier of reeds
with each reed less than three handbreadths from the next, is valid
as Abaye asked of Rabbah.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, חִיצַת הַקָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a new lesson in the source, so it is not obvious.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think the ruling is pointless if the items were made as walls.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that a reed hedge with gaps under three טפחים counts as a wall. So the deflection stands, and רבא is not disproven.

steps.title: Proof from a tree whose branches hang low
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that if a tree's branches hang to within three טפחים of the ground, one may carry under it. The branches act as walls, even though they were not made to be walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A tree that hangs down toward the ground: if its branches are not three handbreadths above the ground, one may carry under it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another proof against רבא, this time from a tree whose branches form walls around the space under it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Branches that come within three טפחים of the ground count as if they reach the ground, through לבוד. Then they enclose the area like walls, so carrying is allowed. A tree does not normally grow in order to be a wall, so this seems to go against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: One may carry. This is about carrying on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: אִילָן הַמֵּסֵיךְ עַל הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: Come and hear: A tree that hangs down over the ground,
if its branches are not higher
than three handbreadths from the ground,
one may carry under it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אִילָן הַמֵּסֵיךְ עַל הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The previous proof was deflected, so the גמרא brings a new one.
steps.raayaObject: That branches not made as walls still count as walls, which goes against רבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about carrying under a low-hanging tree.

steps.title: The tree was planted for this purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא deflects again. The משנה speaks of a tree planted from the start to make an enclosed space.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, what case are we dealing with? Where he planted it from the start for this purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same answer again: the tree was planted to serve as walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner planted the tree so its branches would enclose a space, then the branches are walls made for the purpose. Even רבא agrees those count. So the proof is turned aside.

phrases.english: Here too, with what are we dealing?
where he planted it from the start for this purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the proof of step 13 with the same answer as steps 6 and 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It narrows the משנה to a tree planted on purpose.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the tree was not meant to be a wall. It may have been planted for that reason.

steps.title: Then why is carrying limited to two בית סאה?
steps.stepSummary: If the tree was planted as walls, one should be able to carry in any size area under it. Yet רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits it to a בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, one should be allowed to carry in all of it! Why, then, did רב הונא son of רב יהושע say that one may carry there only in an area of two בית סאה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer. A limit on the size of the area suggests the branches are not treated as full walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real walls built for living around would allow carrying in an area of any size. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits the area under the tree to a בית סאתים, which is the limit for a space not enclosed for living. That limit fits a tree that was not planted for this purpose, so the deflection of step 14 looks weak. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Let one carry in all of it, no matter how big.
Why, then? This points out a contradiction.
An area of two בית סאה, about 5,000 square אמות. It is the limit for carrying in a space not enclosed for living.

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge puts the 'planted for this purpose' answer under pressure. The גמרא must explain the size limit to protect רבא's view.

phrases.english: If so, let one carry in all of it!
Why, then, did Rav Huna
son of Rav Yehoshua say:
One may not carry in it
except in an area of two beit se'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לִיטַלְטֵל בְּכוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges the deflection of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the tree was planted to act as walls.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Walls made for the purpose should allow carrying in any size area. The limit of בית סאתים shows the branches are treated like walls not made for living around.

steps.title: Why the tree area is limited to a בית סאתים
steps.stepSummary: The space under the tree is a דירה שתשמישה לאויר, a dwelling used for the open air outside it. Any such dwelling only allows carrying up to a בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a dwelling used for the open air outside it. In any dwelling like that, you may carry only if it is up to a בית סאתים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15. Even though the tree was planted on purpose as walls, carrying is limited because of what kind of space it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit is not because the walls are weak. The space under the tree is used to watch the fields outside it, not as a real home. The rule for such a space, a דירה שתשמישה לאויר, is that it only allows carrying up to a בית סאתים. So the answer in step 14, that the tree was planted to make an enclosure, still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose use is for the open air outside it, like a watchman's post
An area that can be sown with two סאה of seed, about 5,000 square אמות

steps.confusionAlert: The limit to a בית סאתים does not mean the tree's walls are not real walls. It comes from how the space is used.

phrases.english: Because it is a dwelling
whose use is for the open air outside it,
and any dwelling whose use is for the open air,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין בָּהּ אֶלָּא בֵּית סָאתַיִם.
phrases.english: one may carry in it only if it is up to two beit se'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי דִּירָה שֶׁתַּשְׁמִישָׁהּ לַאֲוִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a separate reason for the size limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בית סאתים limit shows the tree was not planted as walls
steps.terutzMaskana: The limit comes from the rule of a דירה שתשמישה לאויר, not from the walls

steps.title: Proof from a mound, a cavity, and standing grain
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a person who spends שבת on a mound ten טפחים high, in a cavity ten טפחים deep, or in reaped grain surrounded by standing stalks may walk the whole area plus 2,000 אמות. So natural partitions count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Someone spent שבת on a mound ten טפחים high, between four אמות and a בית סאתים in size. Or he spent it in a cavity ten טפחים deep, of the same size. Or he spent it in a reaped field surrounded by standing stalks. He may walk the whole area, and 2,000 אמות beyond it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof that a partition that formed by itself counts as a real מחיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The area counts as one enclosed space, so he may walk all of it plus 2,000 אמות. That only works if its edges count as walls. A mound and a cavity are natural, and nobody built them. So this seems to show that a מחיצה העשויה מאליה counts.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who established his Shabbat place on a mound ten handbreadths high

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְעַד בֵּית סָאתַיִם,
phrases.english: and it is from four cubits up to two beit se'a,
and likewise in a cavity that is ten handbreadths deep,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְעַד בֵּית סָאתַיִם,
phrases.english: and it is from four cubits up to two beit se'a,
and reaped grain with standing stalks surrounding it
he may walk the entire area
and outside it two thousand cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the tree proof was deflected, a new proof is brought
steps.raayaObject: That a מחיצה העשויה מאליה counts as a מחיצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about a תל, a נקע, and קמה

steps.title: The deflection of made on purpose does not work here
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say these were also made on purpose. That could work for the grain, but not for a natural mound or cavity.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too he made it from the start for this purpose: that is fine for the grain. But for a mound and a cavity, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the same escape it used earlier, that the partition was made on purpose. Then it shows the escape fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person could leave stalks standing on purpose to form a wall. A mound and a cavity were always there, though, and nobody made them. So the proof from step 17 stands: natural partitions count.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say, which introduces a possible answer
From the start for this purpose
What is there to say? There is no answer

phrases.english: And if you say that here too
he made it from the outset for this purpose,
granted, for grain that is fine,
but a mound and a cavity
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי שֶׁעָשָׂה מִתְּחִילָּה לְכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks the expected deflection to the proof of step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a מחיצה העשויה מאליה does not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Natural mounds and cavities cannot have been made on purpose, yet they work as walls

steps.title: New framing: everyone agrees on walls, the dispute is about a לחי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier approach. Everyone agrees a natural מחיצה counts. אביי and רבא argue only about a לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: about partitions, everyone agrees that a natural one is a partition. Where they disagree is about a לחי.
steps.whatsHappening: The proofs show natural walls count, so the גמרא changes how it understands the dispute. It sets up the explanation of each side, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא said רבא rejects a self-made מחיצה. The ברייתא disproved that. Now the argument is narrowed to a לחי alone, which may work differently from a wall.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which drops the earlier approach
A side post placed at the opening of a מבוי

phrases.english: Rather: with regard to partitions
everyone agrees
that it is a partition,
where they disagree is about a side post.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בִּמְחִיצוֹת כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the successful proof by reframing the whole dispute
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the subject of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי and רבא argue about a מחיצה העשויה מאליה
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree about walls and argue only about a לחי

steps.title: Why אביי and רבא disagree about a natural לחי
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds that a לחי works as a מחיצה, so a natural one counts. רבא holds that a לחי is a היכר (marker), which only works if a person made it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי follows his own reasoning: a לחי works as a wall, and a wall that formed by itself is a wall. רבא follows his own reasoning: a לחי works as a marker. If it was made by hand, it is a marker. If not, it is not a marker.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each side's reasoning under the new framing. The next steps test this framing against sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute rests on a basic question: what does a לחי do? If it is a kind of wall, a natural one works just like natural walls do. If it is only a sign to remind people, it must be put there by a person. Otherwise it does not signal anything.

keyTerms.meaning: A partition that formed by itself
By hand, made by a person

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees natural walls count. אביי says a לחי is like a wall, so a natural one works. רבא says a לחי is a marker, so it must be made by a person.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea about the nature of a לחי, wall or marker. That question affects many laws of מבוי.

phrases.english: Abaye follows his reasoning, as he said:
a side post works as a partition,
and a partition that formed by itself is a partition.
And Rava follows his reasoning, as he said:
a side post works as a marker,
if it was made by hand it is a marker,
and if not, it is not a marker.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי לְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּאָמַר לֶחִי מִשּׁוּם מְחִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the new framing of step 19
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute about a לחי העומד מאליו depends on whether a לחי is a מחיצה (אביי) or a היכר (רבא)

steps.title: Proof from protruding wall stones
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says stones sticking out of a wall, less than three טפחים apart, count as a לחי. This seems to show that a לחי nobody intended still works, as אביי holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: stones of a wall that stick out from the wall, separated from each other by less than three טפחים, do not need another לחי. If the gap is three, another לחי is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to prove who is right in the argument between אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stones that stick out of a wall were normally not put there to be a לחי. Even so, the ברייתא counts them as one, because gaps under three טפחים are treated as closed (לבוד). That looks like support for אביי, who says a לחי works even if no one intended it.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than three טפחים. A gap this small is treated as closed (לָבוּד).

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Stones of a wall that stick out from the wall
separated from one another by less than three [handbreadths],
there is no need for another side post.
If three, another side post is needed.
phrases.notes: At three טפחים the gap is too wide for the stones to join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אַבְנֵי גָדֵר הַיּוֹצְאוֹת מִן הַגָּדֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the dispute just laid out in step 20 against a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that a לחי works even when it was not made for that purpose

steps.title: The stones were built for this purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The case may be one where the stones were built from the start to serve as a לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is a case where he built them from the start for this purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by reading the ברייתא as a case of a לחי made on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the builder meant the stones to be a לחי, even רבא agrees they work as a marker. So the ברייתא no longer proves anything for אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start for this purpose

phrases.english: Here too
[it is a case] where he built them from the start for this [purpose].

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי שֶׁבְּנָאָן מִתְּחִילָּה לְכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of this ברייתא as a proof for אביי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be talking about stones placed on purpose to be a לחי, which everyone agrees works.

steps.title: Then the ruling is obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the stones were made to be a לחי, why would the ברייתא need to say they count?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading. A deliberately made לחי obviously works, so the ברייתא would be teaching nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is not expected to state something completely obvious. So the reading from step 22 seems to make the ברייתא pointless.

phrases.english: If so, it is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the deflection made in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the stones were built on purpose to be a לחי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that is the case, the ברייתא's ruling adds nothing new.

steps.title: People might think the stones were for joining a building
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that the stones count. Without it, one might think they look like stones left for attaching a future building, so they would not work as a לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that it was made to connect the building [to another building]. So it teaches us [that it still counts as a לחי].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new lesson of the ברייתא even when the stones were made on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Builders sometimes leave stones sticking out so a later building can be attached. Because onlookers would read them that way, one might think they cannot serve as a marker. The ברייתא teaches that if the builder intended them as a לחי, they still work.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. This introduces a mistaken assumption.
To connect the building, meaning to attach another building to it later

phrases.english: You might have said
it was made in order to connect the building [to another].
It teaches us [that it is a valid side post].

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא לְמֵיסַר בִּנְיָינָא הוּא דַּעֲבִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 and keeps the deflection of step 22 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a real lesson for the ברייתא, so it is not stating the obvious
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Stones that look like they were left for a future building would not count as a לחי.
steps.terutzMaskana: If they were made to be a לחי, they count. The proof for אביי is removed.

steps.title: Proof from a wall with a recessed side
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא taught that a wall with one side set back from the other counts as a לחי. This again seems to show that an unintended לחי works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רבי חייא taught: a wall with one side set back from the other, whether the step is seen from outside and even from inside, or seen from inside and even from outside, is treated as a לחי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second proof for אביי from a ברייתא of רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the edge of the alley, the wall narrows, so part of it sticks out a bit past the rest. That sticking-out part is treated as a לחי even though nobody built it for that. This again appears to support אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: That רבי חייא taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
A wall, one side of which is set back from the other,
whether it is visible from outside and even from inside,
or it is visible from inside and even from outside —
it is considered a side post.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a new source for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that a לחי works even when it was not made for that purpose
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי חייא about a wall with a recessed side

steps.title: The wall was also made for this purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again rejects the proof. The wall may have been shaped this way from the start to be a לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is a case where he made it from the start for this purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same move as before. It reads the case as a לחי made on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the step in the wall was made as a לחי, רבא agrees it works. So the ברייתא of רבי חייא does not prove אביי right.

phrases.english: Here too
[it is a case] where he made it from the start for this [purpose].

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ מִתְּחִילָּה לְכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 25, the same way step 22 rejected step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of רבי חייא's ברייתא as a proof for אביי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wall may have been shaped on purpose to serve as a לחי.

steps.title: Then what is the lesson?
steps.stepSummary: If the wall was made to be a לחי, what new thing does the ברייתא teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does it teach us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading. A deliberately made לחי obviously works, so it asks what point the ברייתא is making.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of challenge as step 23. Reading the case as intentional seems to leave the ברייתא with nothing to say.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן?
phrases.english: If so, what does it teach us?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the deflection made in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the wall was shaped on purpose to be a לחי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the ruling seems obvious and the ברייתא teaches nothing.

steps.title: A לחי seen only from outside still counts
steps.stepSummary: The lesson is that a לחי seen from outside but flush with the wall inside still counts as a לחי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: if it is seen from outside and even from inside, it is still treated as a לחי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds the new lesson in the ברייתא, and that lesson has nothing to do with whether the לחי was intended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a לחי is meant to be seen from inside the alley. The new point is that one visible only from outside, and flush on the inside, still works. Since this is a real lesson, the deflection holds, and this ברייתא does not decide between אביי and רבא. The next step brings a new proof from a story about רב.
steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות that seemed to prove אביי can be read as cases where the לחי was made on purpose, so רבא's view still stands. Each ברייתא still has a real lesson: protruding stones count even though they look like they were left for a future building, and a לחי seen only from outside counts.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
if it is visible from outside and even from inside —
it is considered a side post.
phrases.notes: This point is not obvious, since not everyone accepts it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 and keeps the deflection of step 26 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a different real lesson in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the wall was made on purpose, the ברייתא would have nothing to teach.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that a לחי seen only from outside counts. It does not decide between אביי and רבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the standard way the גמרא protects a position. Read the source as a narrower case, then find a fresh lesson so the source is not stating the obvious.

steps.title: The story of רב, the fallen side post, and the palm tree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells a story. רב's לחי fell, and רב stopped his attendant from carrying the water into the מבוי. When רב הונא asked why the palm tree could not count, רב answered that nobody had relied on it since before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב was sitting in a certain alleyway, and רב הונא was sitting in front of him. רב told his attendant, 'Go bring me a jug of water.' By the time the attendant came back, the side post had fallen. רב signaled to him with his hand, and the attendant stopped where he was. רב הונא said to him, 'Doesn't the master hold that we can rely on the palm tree?' רב said, 'This scholar acts like someone who doesn't know the teachings. Did we rely on it since yesterday?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about רב as a new attempt to prove that something not set up as a לחי can still work as one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The palm tree was not planted to be a לחי, yet רב הונא assumed it could count. רב did not reject it because it was a natural tree. He rejected it only because nobody had relied on it before שבת. The next step draws out what this means.

keyTerms.meaning: From yesterday, meaning from before שבת began

steps.confusionAlert: רב did not say the palm tree could never count. He only said it did not count here because nobody had relied on it from before שבת.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rav was sitting in a certain alleyway,
and Rav Huna was sitting before him.
He said to his attendant:
Go, bring me a jug of water.
By the time he came back, the side post fell.
phrases.notes: Without the לחי, carrying into the alleyway would be forbidden.

phrases.english: He signaled to him with his hand, and he stood in his place.
phrases.notes: רב did not want him to carry the water any further.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לִסְמוֹךְ אַדִּיקְלָא?
phrases.english: Doesn't the master hold that one may rely on the palm tree?
phrases.notes: A palm tree stood at the entrance of the alleyway.

phrases.english: He said: This scholar is like
someone who does not know the teachings,
did we rely on it since yesterday?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּרַב הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּהָהוּא מְבוֹאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The proof from רבי חייא's teaching was deflected, so the גמרא brings a new proof, this time from a story.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that a לחי not set up as a לחי still counts
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about רב, רב הונא, and the palm tree in the מבוי

steps.title: Drawing the inference from רב's answer
steps.stepSummary: רב's only reason was that nobody had relied on the tree. So if people had relied on it, the tree would count as a לחי, even though it was never set up as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that we did not rely on it. This implies that if we had relied on it, it would be a לחי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the proof from רב's words: the tree failed only because nobody had relied on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a 'from the reason you can learn the opposite' inference. If reliance would have made the palm tree work, then something not built as a לחי can count. This seems to support אביי against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is. The גמרא is pointing to the exact reason a rule was given.
But this implies; it introduces the opposite case
We relied on it as a לחי

phrases.english: The reason is that we did not rely on it,
but if we had relied on it, it would be a side post.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא — דְּלָא סָמְכִינַן, הָא סָמְכִינַן — הָוֵי לֶחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It completes the proof by drawing a precise inference from רב's answer in the story.
steps.raayaObject: A לחי not set up for that purpose still counts (אביי)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implied flip side of רב's reason: had they relied on the tree, it would count.

steps.title: Suggesting that אביי and רבא agree when the item was relied on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders whether the argument between אביי and רבא is only when people did not rely on the item. If so, everyone would agree that a relied-on item counts, and רב's story would not decide their argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that אביי and רבא argue only when we did not rely on it, but when we did rely on it, it is a לחי according to everyone?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to narrow the argument between אביי and רבא. This would make רב's story fit both views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 placed the dispute where people did rely on the item, but that was under the first framing. Now that the dispute is about whether a לחי is a wall or a marker, the גמרא asks whether they might argue only where nobody relied on it. If so, רב's story deals with a case everyone agrees about and would not prove אביי right.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion the גמרא is testing.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Abaye and Rava
disagree only where we did not rely on it,
but where we did rely on it, it is a side post according to all?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא בִּדְלָא סָמְכִינַן עֲלֵיהּ פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing the inference from רב's story, the גמרא asks whether the argument might be limited so that the story would not decide it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the argument between אביי and רבא apply even when people relied on the item as a לחי from before שבת?

steps.title: The balcony of בר חבו shows they disagree even when relied on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. אביי and רבא argued all their lives about the balcony in בר חבו's house, even though people relied on it. So they disagree even when an item was relied on.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that. There was a certain balcony in the house of בר חבו that אביי and רבא argued about their whole lives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that אביי and רבא agree when people relied on the item. It points to a real case they argued about for years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People relied on the balcony's post as a לחי, yet אביי and רבא still argued about it. So reliance does not end their argument: רבא holds that even a relied-on item does not count. That means רב's story really does stand on אביי's side.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not think that. It firmly rejects a suggestion.
A balcony or porch held up by a post
All their years, meaning their whole lives

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between אביי and רבא applies even when people relied on the item as a לחי. Relying on it alone does not settle it for רבא. Because of this, רב's story leans toward אביי.

phrases.english: Do not let this enter your mind,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָהוּא בַּרְקָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי בַּר חָבוּ
phrases.english: for there was a certain balcony in the house of Bar Chavu
phrases.notes: The residents relied on the post holding up the balcony as their לחי.

phrases.english: about which Abaye and Rava disagreed
all their years.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּהָהוּא בַּרְקָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי בַּר חָבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the narrowing suggestion of the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the idea that אביי and רבא agree when the item was relied on
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion ignores a real case (the balcony of בר חבו) that was relied on, yet they still argued about it for their whole lives.

steps.title: New משנה: a side post may be made from anything, even a living creature
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that a לחי may be made from any material, even a living creature. רבי מאיר forbids using a living creature.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Side posts may be made from anything, even from something that has a living spirit in it. רבי מאיר forbids this.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses what materials may be used to make a לחי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא (first, unnamed opinion) allows any material, even an animal, if it is properly tied in place. רבי מאיר disagrees only about living creatures, which the גמרא will explain later.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. It marks the start of a new משנה.
A living spirit, meaning a living creature

phrases.english: even from something that has a living spirit,
and Rabbi Meir forbids it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בַּכֹּל עוֹשִׂין לְחָיַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier sugya is finished, and a new משנה opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any material, even a living creature, may serve as a לחי. רבי מאיר disagrees about a living creature.

steps.title: A living creature used as a grave covering spreads impurity
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues with a parallel rule. A living creature placed as a גולל (the covering of a grave) passes on טומאה like a regular grave covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it makes things impure as a grave covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second, related case. A living creature used as a grave covering gets the טומאה of a גולל. רבי מאיר's response to this continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same idea as the first clause. A living thing can fill a structural role, so here it can serve as a grave covering and pass on טומאה. The משנה pairs the two cases because the same question about living creatures comes up in both.

keyTerms.meaning: The covering stone of a grave, which passes on טומאה

phrases.english: and it imparts impurity as a grave covering,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It continues the משנה with a parallel case about a living creature.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A living creature used as a grave covering gets the טומאה of a גולל (רבי מאיר's view follows on the next amud).
